answer: A near-duplicate is rejected at the bridge gate and the submitting identity is flagged, so one good text cannot be reused across aliases. Copying an answer therefore yields nothing, and producing 107 genuinely distinct answers per epoch is real inference work with real latency; the relic ledger keeps the similarity graph, and the quartz review can re-run it. Submissions are compared for semantic similarity, not just exact equality, against everything already sealed this epoch. That is 30 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
